today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,007.8, a third consecutive lower settle and -3.66% below last Tuesday's $4,160. The chain stays structurally call-heavy (P/C OI 0.39, 272,269 calls vs 107,002 puts) but that skew is legacy paper parked at $5,500-$8,000 and carries no gravity here. Live structure is the $4,000 put shelf directly under price (5,176 OI) with net GEX at -129 across the +/-20% band and -313 within $200 of spot. ATM IV 21.36% implies a 1-sigma daily move of $53.93 (1.35%), framing $3,954-$4,062.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago this was a long-gamma tape: net window GEX +147.6 on 10/20 with spot pinned in a $17 range across three days. That regime broke on 10/23 when GEX flipped negative (-36.2) and has deepened every session since, reaching -129.2 on 10/26 — dealers are now short gamma through the entire $3,206-$4,809 band, with cumulative net GEX troughing at -607 right at $4,100, directly above spot. The tell is that IV rose into the decline rather than bleeding: ATM IV went 19.91% to 21.36% (+1.45pp) while spot lost $152.2, so the last two down sessions were paid for in premium, not absorbed by it. Max pain finally moved after four days frozen at $5,500, drifting to $5,400 (-$100) as the far call strip erodes, but at +$1,392 above spot it is an artifact of legacy OTM call OI, not a magnet — ignore it and trade the walls. Meanwhile the $3,500 put wall held its strike for all five sessions and gained 425 contracts (5,895 to 6,320), 436 of them added on 10/26 alone: real downside hedging is being bought, not unwound.
what_changed: Net window GEX collapsed +147.6 (10/20) to -36.2 (10/23) to -129.2 (10/26) — short-gamma regime deepening, not stabilizing
ATM IV expanded 19.91% to 21.36% (+1.45pp) across a -$152.2 spot decline — vol bid into weakness, no premium absorption
Max pain broke a four-session freeze at $5,500, drifting to $5,400 (-$100) as far-dated call OI erodes
$3,500 put wall added 425 contracts to 6,320 OI, 436 of them on 10/26 — downside hedges accumulating at the strike, not rolling
P/C OI ratio pinned at 0.39 for all five sessions despite the selloff — the call-heavy skew is inert legacy paper above $5,500
Today's flow split directionally: 1,355 calls at $4,225 and 1,093 at $4,350 against 634 puts at $4,050 and 423 at $4,200
prediction: Bias leans lower while $4,000 caps, with the short-gamma profile guaranteeing that any break gets amplified rather than damped — the cumulative GEX trough at $4,100 means dealer hedging reinforces direction through the whole $3,950-$4,100 pocket. First downside objectives are the $3,950 (4,382 put OI) and $3,900 (5,590 put OI) shelves, a 1-sigma and 2-sigma move respectively. The bearish read is invalidated on a sustained reclaim of $4,062, which is both +1 sigma and last session's $4,060.3 open range; above it the $4,200 gamma flip becomes the real test, and the 2,448 calls traded at $4,225-$4,350 yesterday mark where upside supply sits.
